plan.summary: Nothing new passed the proof rule this week, and the forward logs are still too young (132 closed ideas over 6 dates; Launch picks 3 open, lined-up buys 11 rows). This week's research (groups running together, RS-high dips, EMA touch odds) is built as information, but most of the dashboard's real edge now comes from one idea measured five different ways: a leader dipping into its 9/21 EMAs inside a leading group, best after a thrust. The best next step is the trade warehouse: one table of every setup's past trades, so we can see which of those overlapping layers actually adds edge, show a stacked expected R on each Launch pick and lined-up buy, and drop the ones that only repeat each other.

items.title: Trade warehouse + stacked expected R on Launch picks and lined-up buys
items.where: new module breadth/warehouse.py (start from tools/rstack/box_stack.py); stack line on launchPicksCard and lineupCard; forward log beside data/lineup_ledger.csv
items.how: One table of every past trade from box retests, springs, lined-up dips (lifecycle trigger), Best Setups nuzzles/flags and Launch replays, all on one yardstick (next-open or trigger entry, same R floor, 20 sessions) with the same layer columns. Expected R = setup base + only the lifts we name in advance and that hold in both halves, shrunk by sample size. Each live pick shows its stack, e.g. '+0.30 base, +0.28 leading group, +0.45 thrust window', and the stack is logged and scored forward.
items.test: Lifts fixed before testing: thrust window, leading group (top 30% 60d), lifecycle BUY, SPY above 50-day, in-vogue theme. Each lift = R with minus without, averaged per date, t at least 2 over 20+ dates, same sign both halves. Then score the stacked R on the second half only: top fifth minus bottom fifth must be positive with rank IC at least 0.05.
items.kill: Stacked R doesn't separate second-half trades (IC under 0.05 or top fifth no better than bottom): show the single proven tags only and stop.

items.title: Clean up the 'dip into the 9/21 EMAs' family: keep what adds edge, fold the rest
items.where: layers dips, rspull, emaprob, polished, stairs vs lifecycle (lined-up buys); Setups tab cards
items.how: Six cards flag almost the same trade: an uptrend leader touching its 9/21 EMAs. Alone the touch has no edge (dips ~0, RS-high dips -0.03R, EMA odds -0.07R); the edge only shows inside a leading / BUY group, best after a thrust. Using the warehouse (#1), check how much each one adds beyond lined-up buys; merge the survivors into one 'Into the EMAs' list with tags and drop the rest from the page. That also saves ~100+ seconds of build time (rspull ~50 s, emaprob ~55 s).
items.test: Warehouse trades that pass the lined-up rule: does adding RS-line high, 2nd weekly-EMA touch, stair-step state or Best Setups nuzzle change R? Per date, both halves, t at least 2.
items.kill: If one of them adds at least +0.15R beyond lined-up in both halves, keep it as a tag; otherwise retire its card.

items.title: Market filters on the new headline picks: volume tilt and hidden buying
items.where: lined-up gate (buy / half / hold in lineup.yml and lineupCard); layers volume_tilt, hidden_buying
items.how: Carried over for the third week, now aimed at what Adam actually trades (the old Top 2 is retired). Both gauges predict SPY's next month. If they also change the R of lined-up dips, the gate drops to 'half size' on 'Buyers tiring' or bottom-fifth hidden-buying days. Just two extra warehouse columns.
items.test: Lined-up trigger trades (stock_evidence.trigger, ~750 in BUY groups) by tilt tier and FINRA dev fifth, per date, both halves, t at least 2; repeat inside mixed breadth only so it isn't just the breadth regime again.
items.kill: |t| under 2, halves disagree, or the effect disappears inside one breadth regime.

items.title: Groups running together as an early lifecycle trigger
items.where: lifecycle WATCH to BUY (lifecycle.group_state) and the runners alert in lineup.py
items.how: Running days beat the average group next day (+0.34%, t 2.25) and over 5 days (+0.90%, t 2.47), both halves. WATCH groups alone have no edge, but 53% turn BUY. Test whether a running day in a WATCH or BUY group is the moment to act (or size up), and whether a running day in a 'forgotten' group is just a one-day pop.
items.test: Daily-bar running events split by the group's lifecycle stage that day (no look-ahead), next open to 5 and 20 sessions vs the average group, per date, both halves, t at least 2. Also check the intraday continuation from data/runner_log.csv once ~4 weeks are logged.
items.kill: Running + WATCH no better than running alone, or halves disagree: keep runners as an alert only.

items.title: Earnings season read: UP clusters in BUY groups

items.how: UP clusters lifted the members that hadn't reported (+1.9%, t 1.93, halves agree). The planned test is whether that's stronger when the group is already in BUY. Run it once this earnings season ends (mid-November), when most reports are in.
items.test: UP cluster events, non-reporters next close to 20 sessions vs avg group, split BUY vs not, per date, both halves, t at least 2.
items.kill: No difference with BUY: keep the cluster card as information only.

review.summary: Still too early to judge the news, catalyst and macro-brief layers: only 132 ideas from 6 days (Oct 15-22) have closed, far short of the ~60 ideas over 20+ days the rule needs. The macro-fit backtest (6,382 past setups) again fails: stocks with a recent macro headwind actually did better than those with a tailwind, in both halves, but not by enough to count (t -1.64). The old 5-day swing Top 2 is roughly flat (19 closed, +0.1% avg, 47% winners vs +0.7% for the average candidate). Nothing passed, so nothing should change.
findings: Macro fit (backtest Apr 2025-Oct 2026, 6,382 signals): tailwind +0.47% (n 1,062) vs headwind +1.92% (n 801), t -1.64, both halves negative (-1.0, -1.1 pts). Not proven; info only.
Catalyst positive (forward): +2.7% (n 19) vs -1.1% (n 17), t 0.6, halves disagree (+10.0 / -0.5 pts). Not proven; 6 dates only.
Red flags (forward): no flags +0.8% (n 26) vs flagged +1.2% (n 19), t 0.07, halves disagree. No signal yet.
Earnings inside the hold (forward): clear +2.9% (n 25) vs earnings in hold -1.8% (n 13), t 0.86, both halves same sign but tiny sample. Not proven.
Macro tailwind (forward): 65 vs 1 row, untestable. Macro-brief low risk: 0 low-risk rows, untestable. More support: 5 vs 69 rows, untestable.
No warnings (forward): +3.4% (n 63) vs -1.9% (n 16), no t yet. Interesting direction, sample too small.
By role (132 closed, 5-day vs SPY): pick1 -0.1% (n 6), pick2 +4.1% (n 6), watch +4.2% (n 24), candidates +0.4% (n 96).
Swing Top 2 ledger: 19 closed, avg +0.12% with stops vs +0.69% avg candidate, 47% winners; 9 open, 2 no fill. Setup review flag: off (regime mixed, 20 days since baseline).
proposals: No changes yet: not enough data. Forward log has 132 settled ideas over 6 dates; the rule needs 20+ dates (about mid-to-late November).
Keep macro fit as information only: it failed again (t -1.64). If anything it hints at mean reversion; not worth acting on unless t reaches -2 in both halves.
Watch 'earnings inside the hold' and 'no warnings': both point the expected way; re-check when 20+ dates have settled. Any promotion would still need Adam's approval.

brief.headline: Oil and yields plunged on US-Iran settlement hopes and a Democratic sweep of Congress, with the October jobs report Friday setting up December Fed hike odds.
brief.rates: The 10-year yield fell to about 4.88% (near a two-month low) and the 2-year to about 4.55% as oil dropped and the dollar weakened.
brief.oil: Brent fell about 8.7% to roughly $94.6 and WTI to about $88 on bets that Washington and Tehran are near a settlement, though the Hormuz supply threat is not resolved.
brief.fed: CME FedWatch put a December hike at roughly 80%; the next FOMC is Dec 8-9, and the Friday payrolls print will heavily shape those odds.
brief.geo: US-Iran talks via Qatar continue with no binding deal, and Democrats won both the House and Senate in Tuesday's midterms.

proposals.summary: Checked 50 tickers (4 dead, 20 poor fits, 26 unfiled; HZO skipped: MarineMax is being bought by Safe Harbor Marinas). Biggest fixes: ATKR, BZH and WBD were acquired and should be removed, PSKY became SKYD; ESS is an apartment REIT filed with battery makers, CME belongs with exchanges, ISRG/PRCT are medtech not industrial robots. 25 strong unfiled names (tankers NAT/TEN, GRAL, OSPN, REPX, SG...) get homes.

moves.why: Atkore (conduit and electrical raceway) was bought by Prysmian for about $3.8B; the deal closed Oct 19, 2026 and the stock stopped trading.
Beazer Homes was acquired by Dream Finders Homes (~$2.2B); closed Oct 20, 2026 and delisted. DFH itself is the surviving homebuilder.
Warner Bros. Discovery was acquired by Paramount Skydance (merger closed early Oct 2026); its shares no longer trade. The combined company is SKYD.
Paramount Skydance closed its Warner Bros. Discovery merger in early October 2026 and the combined company, renamed Skydance, trades under the new ticker SKYD.
Essex Property Trust is a West Coast apartment REIT, not a battery maker (ticker mix-up with ESS Tech).
CME Group is the largest futures and options exchange (rates, equity index, energy, ags); crypto futures are a small slice. It trades with ICE/Nasdaq/CBOE.
Intuitive Surgical sells da Vinci surgical systems and instruments to hospitals; it trades like a large medtech, not an industrial robot maker.
PROCEPT BioRobotics sells the Aquablation robotic system for prostate (BPH) surgery to urologists: a medtech device company.
Nordson makes precision dispensing, fluid-management and test/inspection equipment for many industries; not a robotics company.
Rockwell Automation sells factory automation controllers, drives and software (Allen-Bradley); its natural peers are the industrial-automation group.
Lamb Weston makes frozen fries and potato products sold to restaurants and grocers; a food company, not farm equipment.
AES owns regulated utilities (AES Indiana, AES Ohio) plus a large contracted renewables/power business; it trades with defensive utilities, not rooftop solar names.

Sterling's growth engine is E-Infrastructure: site development for data centers and semiconductor fabs; it trades with the AI-buildout contractors (EME, IESC, PWR) far more than civil engineering firms.
DigitalOcean is a cloud provider for developers that now markets itself as an 'agentic inference cloud' with GPU Droplets (AMD MI350X, NVIDIA); it trades with AI-compute names.
Wabtec builds locomotives, rail equipment and transit components; it is an equipment maker, not a railroad carrier like UNP/CSX.
Archrock rents and operates natural-gas compression equipment for producers and midstream pipelines; it trades with midstream gas names.
Legend Biotech's business is Carvykti, a CAR-T therapy for multiple myeloma (with J&J); oncology is its core. Note: takeover chatter makes the chart noisy.
XP is Brazil's largest independent investment platform/broker; it trades with Brazilian/EM financials more than US brokers.
Paysign runs prepaid card programs and payment processing (pharma copay, plasma donor payments).
GRAIL sells Galleri, a blood test for multi-cancer early detection.
Lindblad Expeditions runs expedition cruises (with National Geographic) and adventure travel.
Maravai sells nucleic-acid (mRNA) production reagents and biologics safety testing to drug makers: a tools supplier.
OneSpan sells digital identity, authentication and e-signature security, mainly to banks.
Grid Dynamics provides digital engineering and AI consulting services to enterprises.
Insight Enterprises is an IT solutions integrator (hardware/software resale, cloud and AI services).
Sweetgreen is a fast-casual salad restaurant chain.
Forum Energy Technologies makes drilling, completion and subsea equipment for oil and gas.
Riley Exploration Permian is an oil-weighted Permian Basin producer.
Nordic American Tankers owns Suezmax crude oil tankers.
TEN Ltd (Tsakos Energy Navigation) owns crude, product and LNG tankers.
SELLAS develops galinpepimut-S (WT1 cancer immunotherapy, AML) and other cancer drugs.
Ethos Technologies runs an online life-insurance platform (IPO'd 2026); closest existing group is life insurers.
Eton Pharmaceuticals sells and develops treatments for rare pediatric/endocrine diseases.
AMN Healthcare is the largest US healthcare staffing company (travel nurses, locum doctors), selling to hospitals.
Andersen Group is a tax and advisory firm that IPO'd in Dec 2025; professional services.
Climb Bio develops budoprutug, an anti-CD19 antibody for immune-mediated kidney disease (membranous nephropathy).
Vestis rents uniforms and workplace supplies (Cintas/UniFirst peer), the facility-services group.
Riskified sells AI fraud prevention and chargeback protection to e-commerce merchants.
Porch Group's main business is home insurance (reciprocal exchange) plus software for home inspectors and movers.
Septerna makes oral small-molecule GPCR drugs; its biggest program is an obesity/cardiometabolic deal with Novo Nordisk (up to $2.2B).
MBX Biosciences develops long-acting peptide drugs for endocrine and metabolic disease (canvuparatide for hypoparathyroidism, obesity programs).
Anterix owns 900 MHz spectrum it leases to utilities (Oncor, Ameren, Evergy) for private LTE networks; no exact group, wireless is closest.
Hyperliquid Strategies is a crypto-treasury company holding the HYPE token (~$1.9B); it trades with the ETH treasury names (BMNR, SBET). No altcoin-treasury group exists.
Motorola Solutions makes public-safety radios, land-mobile networks and video security; no better existing group, it just trades like a steady compounder.
Amazon agreed to buy Globalstar at $90/share, so the stock is pinned to the deal price; business is still satellite connectivity. Remove when the deal closes.
Nutanix sells hyperconverged / hybrid-cloud infrastructure software, which is what this group is named for.
Johnson Controls is an HVAC and building-systems company; the current home is exact.
Oracle runs OCI, one of the big AI clouds; recent weakness is about its debt-funded capex, not a wrong group.
Infosys is the anchor of this group; moving it would empty the group.
